claim: The spleen/liver mRNA expression ratio of A5-CE-C7-6 and A5-CE-C10
locus_A: Figure S5, SI p.17 (log axis, 1e0-1e3, no error bars): A5-CE-C7-6 = 16.28, A5-CE-C10 = 5.60, so C7-6 is 2.91x the more spleen-tropic
locus_B: Figure S23A, SI p.35 (linear axis, 0-25, mean+/-s.d., n=3): A5-CE-C7-6 = 11.19, A5-CE-C10 = 11.95, so C10 is marginally the more spleen-tropic
what_we_emitted: NEITHER. Both panels are recorded in 05_values.csv as held, not emitted, and are not pooled.
why: Same quantity, same units, same two lipids, two panels: S23A/S5 is 2.14x for A5-CE-C10 and 0.69x for A5-CE-C7-6, and the RANK INVERTS. Measured, not estimated, by stage01_values.py. The paper never states that these are different experiments or different formulations, and never states that they are the same, so the disagreement cannot be resolved from what we hold. S23A's own error bars reach from ~4 to ~20 on a mean of 12, so the panels may simply both be consistent with enormous between-animal variance - which is itself the reason a ratio of two organ radiances is a poor corpus value.

claim: The number of carbonate tails on an A5-derived lipid
locus_A: SI p.3, general library procedure: "For A3, A4, A5, A6, and A7 derived An-CE-Cm synthesis, 2, 2, 3, 4, and 4 equivalents of alcohols were reacted with the hydroxylamines" - so every A5 member gets 3 equivalents
locus_B: SI p.4, representative syntheses: A5-CE-C5-4, A5-CE-C7-6 and A5-CE-C7-7 were each made with the core at 0.5 equivalent of the alcohol, i.e. 2 equivalents of alcohol per core, and their HRMS confirms 2 tails (577.4422 / 689.5674 / 717.5987, all reproduced here to <=0.075 ppm)
what_we_emitted: Per-lipid tail counts taken from HRMS where it exists: 3 for the linear C8/C9/C10 members (0.33 eq core = 3 eq alcohol, SI p.3) and 2 for the branched C5-4/C7-6/C7-7 members.
why: The general procedure describes the CRUDE library used for the initial screen; the representative syntheses describe PURIFIED single compounds made at tailored stoichiometry. The paper does not say the library members have the same tail count as their purified namesakes. This is why the five Figure S5 lipids with no HRMS carry structure_assumed=1 and confidence=medium: the branched-means-2-tails rule is an inference from three anchored siblings, not a statement the paper makes.

locus_A: Figure S16, SI p.28 DRAWS two of them in full: "A5-CE-C8 4-tails control" and "A5-CE-C5-4 3 tails control"
locus_B: Figures S14/S15, SI pp.26-27 give HRMS and 1H NMR for DIFFERENT ones: "A5-CE-C9 lipid control with four tails" (917.7036) and "A5-CE-C7-6 lipid control with three tails" (915.7607); Figure S17, SI p.29 MEASURES four others: C9 4-tails, C10 4-tails, C7-6 3-tails, C7-7 3-tails
what_we_emitted: Only the two with HRMS are enumerated (A5-CE-C9-4tails, A5-CE-C7-6-3tails). The two drawn in S16 are not enumerated and carry no value.
why: The two compounds the SI draws are the two it never characterises and never quantifies; the ones it characterises are not the ones it draws. Not necessarily an error - S16's purpose is to illustrate the tail-number concept - but it means a reader who builds structures from the drawn panel gets two molecules that appear in no measurement.

locus_A: Figures S5, S17B and S23A label the y axis "Average radiance efficiency (Spleen / Liver)"
locus_B: Figure S24 labels its y axis "Avg Radiance [p/sec/cm2/sr]"
what_we_emitted: The axis label verbatim per panel, in 05_values.csv's assay column.
why: Radiance and radiance EFFICIENCY are different IVIS quantities - efficiency divides by the incident excitation power and is a fluorescence quantity, while bioluminescence is reported as radiance. For a RATIO of two organs the normalisation cancels, so S5/S17B/S23A are internally fine, but the mixed terminology means we cannot assume S24's absolute numbers are on the same footing as the ratio panels' numerators.

locus_A: The lit_review tracker records 161 lipids for this paper
locus_B: The SI names exactly 15 distinct An-CE-Cm structures (11 in Figure S5, plus 2 extra-tail controls and 2 carboxylate analogs), gives HRMS for 10 of them, and draws 4 in full. It never states a library size.
what_we_emitted: 15 structures enumerated; 0 of the remaining ~146 are namable from what we hold.
why: Not a contradiction in the paper - the library size is presumably stated in the main text, which is paywalled and which we do not hold. Recorded so the gap between the tracker's 161 and this folder's 15 is explicit rather than looking like an extraction failure.

claim: RETRACTED SUSPICION: that Figure S22C's bar baseline is image row 440
locus_A: A dark-row scan of the full page-34 image returned rows 54, 55 and 440 as spanning >25% of the image width, and 440 was taken as panel C's axis rule
locus_B: Repeating the scan over panel C's own x range (1120-1400) returns rows 379-380 only; row 440 is panel A's flow-cytometry box, 60 px lower. Panel C's rule at 379.5 coincides with its own detected 1e4 tick at 379.93, delta 0.43 px
why: Error class 20 - an origin anchored on a panel box rather than on detected ticks - caught by check P6 on its first run. All 23 digitised values were byte-identical before and after the correction, verified by diffing 01_digitised.json, because every bar top (rows 197-281) lies far above both candidate baselines. The guard was aimed at the wrong line; the measurements were not affected.

claim: RETRACTED SUSPICION: that a C10 anchor whose hand-typed SMILES is byte-identical to the enumeration output is a copy
locus_A: make_reference.py's first version raised SystemExit on byte-identity, and 2 of its 4 hand-transcribed anchors (A5-CE-C7-6, A5-C7-6) are byte-identical to stage02_structures.py's canonical output
locus_B: CLAUDE.md section 6: byte-identity of the EMITTED anchor is not the signal and testing for it is a trap, because a correct re-derivation canonicalises to the same string as a correct enumeration - which is precisely why C10's own anchor_may_be_a_copy missed F-037
what_we_emitted: The byte-identity is reported as information. Independence is asserted instead on the GENERATOR'S TEMPLATE, by an AST check that every anchor SMILES is a source string literal and that the module imports no assembler.
why: Retired by the project's own written rule plus the measurement that 2 of 4 demonstrably independent transcriptions collide byte-for-byte. The original guard would have forced a correct anchor to be rewritten into a worse one until its bytes differed. The replacement check was seeded (an anchor SMILES changed from a literal to a .replace() call) and exits 1.
